tool.name: HyphAeon-Epistasis
tool.description: Phylogenetic branch co-selection & epistatic sector mining
tool.command: @SYMLINK_FILES@ hyphaeon epistasis -a input.$input_file.extension @INPUT_TREE@ @MODEL_SOURCE@ #if $focal_taxon: --focal-taxon '$focal_taxon' #end if --min-sim $min_sim --min-shared $min_shared --max-fdr $max_fdr --min-lrt $min_lrt --min-clique-size $min_clique_size --max-overlap $max_overlap --min-coherence $min_coherence --n-permutations $n_permutations #if $max_perm_p: --max-perm-p $max_perm_p #end if $no_dms @OUTPUTS@ #if $graphml_output: --graphml '$graphml_out' #end if

param.name: focal_taxon
param.label: Focal taxon (optional)
param.help: Taxon name for focal-species signature extraction within sectors. If omitted, consensus signatures are reported.

param.label: Min cosine similarity
param.help: Pairwise cosine similarity threshold for declaring a co-selection edge between two sites

param.label: Min shared branches
param.help: Minimum number of shared mutated phylogenetic branches required for a co-selection edge

param.label: Max FDR q-value
param.help: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR q-value threshold for retaining co-selection edges

param.label: Min site LRT
param.help: Minimum site selection drive (LRT) for a site to be considered as a sector seed

param.label: Min clique size
param.help: Minimum clique seed size for initiating epistatic sector growth

param.label: Max sector overlap
param.help: Maximum Jaccard overlap allowed between discovered sectors (higher = more overlapping sectors permitted)

param.label: Min spectral coherence
param.help: Minimum spectral coherence ratio C(S) for epistatic sectors

param.label: Monte Carlo permutations
param.help: Number of random K-site subset Monte Carlo permutations for sector significance testing

param.label: Max permutation p-value (optional)
param.help: Maximum permutation p-value threshold to retain sectors (default: None, retain all C(S) >= min_coherence)

param.label: Skip DMS sweep
param.help: Skip the 19-amino-acid in silico Selection DMS sweep (faster, but no per-site plasticity scores)

param.name: graphml_output
param.label: Export GraphML network
param.help: Export the co-selection network to GraphML for visualization in Cytoscape or Gephi

tool.help:
HyphAeon Epistasis: Branch Co-Selection & Epistatic Sector Mining =======================================================================
**What question does this method answer?**
Which groups of codon sites have historically co-mutated along the same phylogenetic branches, suggesting epistatic coupling? What are the discrete "sectors" of co-evolving residues in a protein?
**How it works**
HyphAeon parses shared evolutionary branch histories to find pairs of sites that show correlated selection signals across the tree. These co-selection edges are filtered by cosine similarity, shared-branch count, and FDR correction, then assembled into "Epistatic Sectors" — networks of residues that historically mutate together. A two-stage seed-and-extend algorithm grows sectors from cliques of mutually co-selected sites.
**Why this matters for drug resistance**
Primary resistance mutations often incur a fitness cost that is rescued by distant compensatory (allosteric) mutations. If a primary escape mutation is identified in the active site (via DMS), the epistatic network highlights the distant structural loops that the pathogen is evolutionarily pre-wired to mutate next, enabling preemptive combination therapy design.
**Inputs**
- An in-frame codon alignment (FASTA or NEXUS) - An optional phylogenetic tree - A focal taxon (optional, for focal-species signature extraction)
**Outputs**
- **JSON**: full results including co-selection edges (with CESI scores, FDR q-values), discovered sectors (with spectral coherence, PARS signatures), and per-site plasticity (if DMS sweep is not skipped) - **CSV**: tabular per-site summary - **GraphML**: co-selection network for visualization in Cytoscape/Gephi
**Key parameters**
- *Min cosine similarity*: threshold for declaring two sites co-selected (lower = more edges, noisier; higher = fewer, more confident edges) - *Min shared branches*: how many independent branch events must show co-mutation (higher = more robust to founder effects) - *Max FDR*: false discovery rate threshold for edge retention - *Min clique size*: smallest seed clique to start growing a sector (smaller = more, smaller sectors; larger = fewer, more cohesive sectors) - *Max overlap*: Jaccard overlap allowed between sectors (lower = more distinct sectors; higher = more overlapping)
